open_points.subject: model_fields.model_items model recognition
open_points.text: For a model, its declared fields as name and value pairs in their declared order, a nested model given as a value and not opened; for any other value, that it is no model.
open_points.question: Does “a model” mean only an instance of a model emitted from this specification, also a subclass of one, or every Pydantic model instance?
options: Only exact emitted Registry model classes count.
Emitted Registry model classes and their subclasses count, but only specification-declared fields are returned.
Every Pydantic model instance counts and its Pydantic-declared fields are returned.
open_points.default_guess: Only instances of emitted Registry model classes count; unrelated Pydantic models and subclasses that add undeclared fields are answered as no model.

witness.initial: A caller holds an instance of a Pydantic model that is not declared in Registry's specification.
events: module:owner_interface calls module:model_fields.model_items with that value.
outcomes: model_items answers that the value is no model.
model_items returns the foreign model's fields as ordered name/value pairs.
witness.observer: module:owner_interface and the rendered owner page

open_points.subject: models emitter and model_fields integration
open_points.text: Every generic walk of a model takes its fields here and nowhere else:
open_points.question: How will model_fields obtain the specification-declared model identity, field order and values from the emitted models without making callers inspect them directly?
options: Generate a closed registry mapping each emitted model class to ordered field accessors.
Emit specification metadata on every model and have model_fields read that metadata.
Generate explicit per-model branches inside model_fields.
consequences: A closed registry makes recognition and ordering explicit but must be regenerated whenever models change.
Emitted metadata keeps model knowledge beside each class but enlarges the emitter's public convention with model_fields.
Explicit branches avoid a metadata protocol but duplicate model knowledge in generated code and require exhaustive regeneration.
open_points.requirement: For a model, its declared fields as name and value pairs in their declared order, a nested model given as a value and not opened; for any other value, that it is no model.
open_points.default_guess: Generate a closed registry of emitted model classes with ordered field accessors.

open_points.subject: models import declaration
open_points.text:
The module is emitted,
not generated: the Factory's models emitter writes it from the
specification's `models` and writes its own imports, pydantic's base model
class among them, so the specification declares no import for it and
`imports.third_party_by_module` names only generated modules.
open_points.rule: `stdlib_by_module` и `third_party_by_module` — module → список полных import строк, необходимых конкретному модулю. Для записи в этих таблицах projector обязан перенести import в local spec без поиска имени библиотеки в notes или contracts. Глобальные `stdlib`/`third_party` остаются каталогом допустимых imports; module-scoped таблицы являются структурным доказательством необходимости.
open_points.question: The passage must declare the emitted `models` module's required Pydantic import in `third_party_by_module`, rather than excluding the module because the emitter writes the import.
